subject: Difference in non-wear hours estimates between Part5 Day Summary and Person Summary output

messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Difference in non-wear hours estimates between Part5 Day Summary and Person Summary output
parts:
Hi there,

I have analysed my GENEActiv dataset and requested the Part5 output to be calculated in midnight-midnight window frame. When I looked at the 'non-wear hours' column in the Part5-Day Summary, I saw '0' for all the recording days and thus I assumed that my participants never took the device off? However, when I looked at the 'nonwear_hours_pla' column in the Part5-PersonSummary, there were few hours recorded for the participants (Please refer to attached file for an example). Could anyone please tell me why is that such a big difference between the two output and which one should I be looking at for the more accurate results (I assumed Part5-Day Summary?)?

messages.author: fe461312361bc741
messages.subject: Re: Difference in non-wear hours estimates between Part5 Day Summary and Person Summary output
parts:
Hi John,

your day summary actually includes one or a couple of days of non-wear time for each participant, which explains an average of about 3,4h across the week. Have you tried WW instead of MM? You could also set maxdur = 7, which should get rid of your 8th day.

Regards,
David

messages.subject: Re: Difference in non-wear hours estimates between Part5 Day Summary and Person Summary output
parts:
Hi David,

Thanks for your suggestion. For Part5 output I supposed it includes only days with the minimum valid hours (16 hours) and thus, in my case, only the first 6 days were included in the calculation? And as per DaySummary output, the non-wear hours were zero for the first 6 days of all participants. That's why I was surprised to see about 3 hours of non-wear time appeared in the PersonSummary output. Does it make sense to you?

Thanks and best regards,
John.

messages.author: fe461312361bc741
messages.subject: Re: Difference in non-wear hours estimates between Part5 Day Summary and Person Summary output
parts:
Hi John,


it does. However, the manual says: 
includedaycrit
minimum required number of valid hours in day specific analysis (NOTE: there is no minimum required number of hours per day in the summary of an entire measurement, every available hour is used to make the best possible inference on average metric value per week)

I am not sure about an optimal solution with regard to non-wear time. It might actually be better to only average it, if there are periods of wear time following the non-wear periods, which reminds me of bout.metric = 4.

Have you tried adjusting maxdur?

Regards,
David
